title: Next multi-stream loop draft
first_prompt:

commits.summary: Observation specs per entry point (foundations O1, step 1): lib/src/observations.rs, jvmcontract observations, and observe::entry_points
commits.body: The observations stream's first step. A new module reads the boundary analysis's facts into the shared IR as one EntryPointSpec per route, message listener, schedule and application-event listener: a stable id (POST /quotes, kafka TOPIC, schedule ARGS, event TYPE), the external inputs with how each is bound (identity derivations: both versions get the same request), the result, exception and a route's status per outcome, one effect observation per modeled call with the payload paths it snapshots at the call, each effect site with its transaction placement, the identity policy, the environment model (every modeled call, outcome 'returns', trace bound 4, exact order, its restriction stated as an assumption) and what the analysis can't see, named (dynamic call sites such as string concatenation, calls it can't follow, computed targets, framework-supplied parameters). reach.rs records each effect's call site for it; the boundary contract's text is unchanged. New command 'jvmcontract observations PATHS [--json]'.

commits.summary: Observation specs for every Box Office entry point (foundations O1, step 2), with sibling modules followed
commits.body: jvmcontract observations now gives a spec for each of Box Office's 13 routes, listeners and schedules (ticketing-service 9, payment-service 3, messaging 1). They were checked by hand against the source and the boundary contracts, and that check found three bugs, now fixed. First, the walk didn't enter sibling modules, so the outbox and inbox writes, the placement inside Transactions.run and the guards' 500s were missing. observations::analyse now takes the entry-point classes and the followed classes as two sets, as boundaries::analyse_in does, and the command takes --base DIR, as verify does. Second, a Class argument was expanded into the document's fields as payload; reach.rs now keeps a class literal's declared type. Third, a method inherited from the library (Enum.ordinal) was named unresolved; it is now a library call. The trace bound is now at least the number of effect sites.

commits.summary: Two builds' observation specs compared into accounted obligations (foundations O2, step 1): observations::compare and observations --against
commits.body: observe::compare, which returned a named Unsupported since Phase 0, now matches the entry points of two builds by what their consumers address: verb and route with path variable names erased, topic or queue, schedule. A renamed handler is the same entry point. A renamed route is one entry point removed and one new, with the handler that now serves the new route named, because only a person can say the route change is intended. Every observation of every old entry point gets exactly one obligation: preserved (to prove; the shapes agree, which discharges nothing), changed (a status mapping, a payload path, an effect moved into or out of a transaction or to another target, the response type), removed, or unresolved (an unknown status, or entry points a key can't tell apart). Two more obligations sit beside them: 'inputs', for a change to the external inputs, which belong to the preservation contract, and 'unresolved', for what the analysis can't see. Each obligation says what discharging it needs. observations::unaccounted checks that the accounting is complete. New option: jvmcontract observations ... --against OLD.json. Obligation gained new_entry, differences and needs, all with serde defaults.
